preamble: The voiceless lateral affricate [tɬ] loses its stop closure and voicelessness to become the plain lateral [l]. In the Nahuan languages the /tɬ/ created by Whorf's law (Proto-Uto-Aztecan *t before *a) became /l/ in western varieties such as Michoacán Nahuatl, alongside the eastern change to /t/; Mexican Spanish shows the same outcome in a few loanwords with final -tl.

examples.note: Both the initial and the final (absolutive) /tɬ/ appear as /l/; Michoacán Nahuatl has no /tɬ/ phoneme.
Compare Morelos Nahuatl tlaxkale and Tetelcingo Nahuatl tlaxcali̱, which keep tl.
Word-final [tɬ] adapted as [l]; more often Spanish gave -te (élotl > elote, pétatl > petate).
